title: Composition of normalized unshifted rational Tate-line comparisons
statement: For a prime l, a finite rational coefficient index c or the algebraic-closure index, and composable scheme arrows f:X→Y and g:Y→Z with l invertible in every residue field of X,Y,Z, let Λ=(coefficient l c).X and L_A=line l c A as in [def-sfb-rational-tate-pullback-comparison]. Then the canonical underived internal-module compositor c_f,g:(f≫g)*≅g*⋙f*, followed by f* of lineComparison(g) and lineComparison(f), equals lineComparison(f≫g). This is an equality of unshifted module maps, before taking degree-zero complexes, derived functors, shifts, exchange mates or adjunction units.

source.place: Roots of unity; The integral twist; Rational and algebraic closure, applied to two successive pullbacks. Also canonical-map composition compatibility in the second rational P1 triangle.

proof.text: Use the normalized linePullIso adjunct equation from linePull_existsUnique. Transpose the iterated module composite using homEquiv_comp_conjugateEquiv_app and conjugateIsoEquiv_upperStarComp. Naturality of the two adjunction bijections, lowerStar_map_hom, and lowerStarComp_hom_app_hom identify its forgotten adjunct with the iterated abelian adjunct. Thus any composition equation for the normalized abelian comparisons gives the required module equation by faithfulness and injectivity of the adjunction.

The abelian compositor is conjugate to the pushforward compositor. For coefficients, condensedPushforwardHom_comp and injectivity of adjunction give the pullback composition equation. For roots, transpose and use existsUnique_proEtaleRootsOfUnityDirectImageMap: on each section the composite is restriction through the two pullback projections and the canonical pullback associativity map. The equation Over.pullbackComp_left_fst_fst identifies their composite with the single projection, and functoriality of appTop identifies the restrictions.

Monoidality of the abelian inverse-image compositor and naturality of its tensor comparison show that composition of tensor comparisons is the tensor product of the two composite comparisons. Apply the projection equations integralComparison_π for f, g and f≫g. The compositor naturality square moves each finite projection through the two successive pullbacks; the coefficient and root composition laws give equality at that level. The preserved-limit hom_ext lemma integral_maps_ext proves equality of integral comparisons.

For a finite field E, precompose with the inverse image of the scalar-extension quotient Mod.extendπ, which is epimorphic. The rational_scalar equations give the corresponding naturality squares. Pasting these squares expresses the iterated rational comparison on the quotient as the tensor product of the coefficient and integral iterated comparisons followed by the target quotient. The tensor composition equation and the preceding integral equation identify this with rational_scalar for f≫g. Cancel the epimorphism.

For Qbar, use preservation by inverse image of the actual abelian finite-field colimit and its hom_ext principle. Paste the qbar_coprojection squares for f and g; each finite-field component is the rational composition equation followed by the target coprojection. The qbar_coprojection equation for f≫g gives equality on all components. Finally split the coefficient index and apply the module lifting argument of step 1. The private abelianComparison selector identifies each branch with its existing rational or closure map; the normalization helper unfolds lineComparison while keeping the large coefficient structures folded.

lean.statement:
theorem lineComparison_comp
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (c : Option (PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField l))
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)]
    [∀ x : Y, Invertible (l : Y.residueField x)]
    [∀ x : Z, Invertible (l : Z.residueField x)] :
    (CondensedRing.upperStarComp (coefficient l c).X f g).hom.app (line l c Z) ≫
        (CondensedRing.upperStar (coefficient l c).X f).map (lineComparison l c g).hom ≫
        (lineComparison l c f).hom = (lineComparison l c (f ≫ g)).hom
